introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Question 3 : dans l'enonce imprime, « where = i + 5j - 3k » : le symbole a est absent du scan. Il est reconstitue en a = i + 5j - 3k a partir de « the position vectors of A, B and C are a, b and c » ; signale entre crochets dans l'enonce et le corrige.

Question 3 (a) : la forme imprimee r = a + tb ne peut designer que la direction de AB (b - a) ; le corrige donne r = a + t(b - a) et montre que la lecture litterale (b = vecteur position de B) ne donnerait pas la droite AB.

questions.enonce_markdown: The position vectors of the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ respectively, where $\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}$ [the symbol $\mathbf{a}$ is missing in the scan, which reads "where = i + 5j - 3k"; it is reconstructed from "position vectors ... are a, b and c"], $\mathbf{b} = -3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 7\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{c} = \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$. Given that $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, find an equation of the line $AB$, in the form $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + t\mathbf{b}$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The reconstructed data are $\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}$ [reconstructed], $\mathbf{b} = -3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 7\mathbf{k}$, $\mathbf{c} = \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$.

The line passes through $A$ and has direction $\overrightarrow{AB}$:

$$\overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a} = (-3 - 1)\mathbf{i} + (-1 - 5)\mathbf{j} + (7 + 3)\mathbf{k} = -4\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} + 10\mathbf{k}.$$

$$\boxed{\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + t(\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}) = (\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}) + t(-4\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} + 10\mathbf{k})}$$

or, with a shorter direction vector, $\mathbf{r} = (\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}) + s(-2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k})$ (with $s = 2t$).

**Remark on the printed form.** The question asks for the form $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + t\mathbf{b}$, where the letter $\mathbf{b}$ can only stand for a direction vector (the direction of $AB$, equal to $\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$ here). It cannot mean the position vector $\mathbf{b}$ of $B$: the line $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + t\mathbf{b}$ would need $-3 = 1 - 3t$ and $-1 = 5 - t$, that is $t = \frac43$ and $t = 6$ at once, so it does not even pass through $B$.

Check: $t = 1$ gives $(1 - 4, 5 - 6, -3 + 10) = (-3, -1, 7)$, which is $B$.

questions.enonce_markdown: The position vectors of $A$ and $B$ are $\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}$ [reconstructed] and $\mathbf{b} = -3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 7\mathbf{k}$. Given that $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, find the position vector of $M$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The position vector of the midpoint of $AB$ is the mean of the position vectors of $A$ and $B$:

$$\overrightarrow{OM} = \frac{\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}}{2} = \frac{(1 - 3)\mathbf{i} + (5 - 1)\mathbf{j} + (-3 + 7)\mathbf{k}}{2} = \frac{-2\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}}{2}.$$

$$\boxed{\overrightarrow{OM} = -\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}}$$

Check: $M = (-1, 2, 2)$ lies on the line of part (a) with $t = \frac12$: $(1 - 2,\ 5 - 3,\ -3 + 5) = (-1, 2, 2)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the Cartesian equation of the plane $ABC$, where $\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k}$ [reconstructed], $\mathbf{b} = -3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + 7\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{c} = \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two vectors in the plane:

$$\overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a} = -4\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} + 10\mathbf{k}, \qquad \overrightarrow{AC} = \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{a} = 0\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} + 3\mathbf{k}.$$

A normal vector is their vector product:

$$\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ -4 & -6 & 10 \\ 0 & -4 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = \mathbf{i}(-18 + 40) - \mathbf{j}(-12 - 0) + \mathbf{k}(16 - 0) = 22\mathbf{i} + 12\mathbf{j} + 16\mathbf{k}.$$

Divide by $2$: $\mathbf{n} = 11\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j} + 8\mathbf{k}$.

The plane is $\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{n} = \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{n}$, with $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{n} = 11(1) + 6(5) + 8(-3) = 11 + 30 - 24 = 17$. Therefore

$$\boxed{11x + 6y + 8z = 17}$$

Check with the other points: $B(-3, -1, 7)$: $-33 - 6 + 56 = 17$. $C(1, 1, 0)$: $11 + 6 + 0 = 17$. $M(-1, 2, 2)$: $-11 + 12 + 16 = 17$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the value of the constant $a$ for which the line $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k} + \lambda(2\mathbf{i} + a\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})$ is parallel to the plane $ABC$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plane $ABC$ has normal vector $\mathbf{n} = 11\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j} + 8\mathbf{k}$ (part (c)). The line is parallel to the plane exactly when its direction vector $\mathbf{d} = 2\mathbf{i} + a\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{n}$:

$$\mathbf{d}\cdot\mathbf{n} = 22 + 6a + 8 = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 6a = -30.$$

$$\boxed{a = -5}$$

The line is parallel to the plane but does not lie in it: the point $(0, 1, 2)$ of the line gives $11(0) + 6(1) + 8(2) = 22 \neq 17$.
